gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each named board costs at its maker's own store on 2026-11-21, where the MCHOSE Ace 60 Pro lists from $37.40 (ChatGPT's card said $58.65), the Epomaker HE68 Lite is $42.49 (ChatGPT's Newegg card said $44.49), and Gamakay's NS68 starts at $36.79, below both.
standout_why: Compared against mechanicalkeyboard.net (best-budget-hall-effect-keyboard), gamepadsquire.com, mkbguide.com (under-100), hlplanet.com and setupinsider.com, all opened 2026-11-21. Every one except mkbguide already prints prices, and HLPlanet (cited in chat 1) already lists the Gamakay NS68 at $42.99 as its cheapest wireless option, the NS75 at $79.99 and the TK75HE V2 at $89.99. What they lack is prices read today: their figures are pre-Black-Friday (HE68 Lite $49.99 on mechanicalkeyboard.net, $39.99-$42 on gamepadsquire; MCHOSE Ace 60 $49.99 on HLPlanet), and none shows the Ace 60 Pro near $37 or the NS75 at $63.99. None gives a measured latency for any board except HLPlanet's 0.3 ms for the MCHOSE Ace 68. A dated price table is a refresh of what rivals have, not a new deciding fact. I could not open the Attack Shark or ATK stores, so the table is incomplete for three of ChatGPT's nine picks.
decides: It confirms rather than changes the pick: on today's maker prices the wired compact boards ChatGPT led with (MCHOSE Ace 60 Pro from $37.40, Epomaker HE68 Lite $42.49, Epomaker HE65 V2 TMR $59.99) all sit well under $100, so price does not separate them and layout and connection do. All four Gamakay boards are under budget: NS68 from $36.79 (65%), NS75 $63.99, TK75HE V2 $79.19 and TK75 TMR $89.99 (all 75%, tri-mode). The honest segment for ours is a 75% board with function row, knob and wireless at $63.99, against wired-only function-row picks (Redragon K707 HE $49.99 wired per Redragon; Royal Kludge C84 $74.99 and Attack Shark R85 HE wired per mechanicalkeyboard.net and gamepadsquire). That segment claim still needs Gamakay's per-mode polling figure, which I could not read (store returned HTTP 429). One caution for the page: MonsGeek's own FUN60 Ultra page read as 'Unavailable' with a waitlist on 2026-11-21, but I could not confirm stock per variant, so do not state it as fact without a re-read.
